answer: Separate batch and speed paths (Lambda) have two code paths with the same business logic written twice, which drifts over time. Correctness comes from the batch overwrite, so reprocessing means rerunning the batch job, and the serving layer merges the two at the boundary hour, where totals can disagree when the layers are out of step. A single job definition that runs bounded or unbounded (Kappa/converged) has one code path, one set of tests, and one deploy. Correctness comes from handling late data in the stream, reprocessing is a replay of the retained log through the same job, and there is one output table with no merge. It requires log retention long enough to replay, and late events must be handled well.
